sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant experimental systematic uncertainties reported by ATLAS for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios?
How do uncertainties in B-meson production fractions and fragmentation affect ATLAS branching ratio determinations?
sub_answers.text:
Uncertainties of relative branching fractions include statistical uncertainties, internal experimental systematic uncertainties, uncertainties from external measured branching ratios, and uncertainties from unmeasured branching ratios [d141416s0p0].
The measured production-related branching fraction can have an additional uncertainty due to the measured parent-hadron transverse momentum spectrum [d141416s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What theoretical inputs (e.g., decay constants, form factors) and their uncertainties enter the interpretation of B→μμ results?
sub_answers.text:
Decay constants and transition form factors enter interpretations of heavy-to-light and semileptonic decays [d10721s0p0].
The numerical values and momentum dependence of these form factors are sensitive to model parameters such as wave-function beta parameters [d10721s0p0].
Lattice calculations and experimental measurements are used to fix some parameters and reduce uncertainties in form factors and decay constants [d10721s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do differences among experiments or analysis methods create tensions or ambiguities in combined B→μμ constraints?
sub_answers.text:
Measured branching fractions can be compatible with Standard Model predictions with consistency levels that vary between about 1.4σ and 3.8σ depending on model assumptions and analysis choices [d125855s0p0].
Measurements of lepton-flavour-universality ratios can reach different precisions and systematic uncertainties, producing differing levels of agreement with the Standard Model across kinematic regions [d122078s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What model-dependent assumptions (e.g., effective operator basis, lepton-flavor universality) lead to ambiguous theoretical interpretations?
sub_answers.text: Tests of lepton-flavour universality are an explicit model assumption when comparing muon and electron decay channels in B decays [d122078s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS measurements of B→μμ branching ratios are used to constrain new coupling parameters controlling scalar and pseudoscalar contributions in models with vector-like fermions and scalar leptoquarks [d72444s0p0].
Leptoquark constructions aimed at addressing b→sμ+μ− anomalies are tested against ATLAS branching-ratio results to limit parameter space that would induce large scalar or pseudoscalar effects [d71088s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
sub_answers.text:
Scalar leptoquark models are constrained by ATLAS B→μμ branching-fraction measurements through limits on their couplings and masses [d72444s0p0].
Muon-flavored leptoquark scenarios designed to address b→sμ+μ− anomalies are tested and limited by ATLAS dimuon and related searches [d71088s0p0].
Models with new neutral gauge bosons (Z′) that produce b→sℓℓ effects and models with vector-like fermions are also constrained by ATLAS searches and branching-ratio limits relevant to b→sμμ observables [d37511s0p0][d60942s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
sub_answers.text:
Higher integrated luminosity and future LHC configurations will increase muon rates and, together with detector upgrades, preserve or improve sensitivity to rare dimuon decays enabling stronger constraints on flavor-violating couplings [d121223s0p0].
Improved experimental precision and reduced systematic uncertainties from LHC measurements and related inputs will sharpen fits and strengthen exclusions of new-physics parameter space [d51548s0p0].

Which specific muon reconstruction and identification algorithms (e.g., Combined, Standalone, Segment-tagged, Muid/STACO, inner-detector matching, isolation/quality working points) does ATLAS apply when reconstructing the low-rate B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− signal, and what operating points or track/vertex-quality selections are reported for these analyses?
sub_answers.text: The ATLAS muon spectrometer provides precision muon momentum measurements with about 50 micron tracking resolution to |eta|<2.7 and momentum resolution of roughly 4% at 100 GeV rising to 10% at 1 TeV [d12480s0p0]. The ATLAS muon triggering and precision tracking use dedicated trigger chambers and precision Muon Drift Tube (MDT) chambers, and plans exist to use MDT data in a highly selective first-level muon trigger for improved momentum discrimination at high rates [d32191s0p0]. The ATLAS inner pixel detector is the innermost tracking device and largely defines the experiment's ability to resolve primary and secondary vertices and perform efficient flavor tagging needed for rare B decays [d6341s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What precise event preselection cuts and multivariate discriminator strategies did ATLAS adopt to separate B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− signal from background — including the full list of input features, the classifier type(s) (BDT, NN, likelihood), training samples, cross-validation scheme, score selection thresholds, and any separate category definitions (e.g., barrel/endcap, trigger categories)?

How does ATLAS construct models for the dominant combinatorial background and for peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− searches — specifically, what background sources are considered (e.g., misidentified B→h+h−, semileptonic decays, partially reconstructed B decays), what data-driven control samples or MC templates are used, and how are misidentification rates and normalization factors measured and propagated?

What exact fitting framework and statistical model does ATLAS use to extract signal yields and branching fractions in B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− analyses — for example, unbinned/ binned extended maximum-likelihood fits, simultaneous fits across categories, the analytic PDF choices for signal and backgrounds (Crystal Ball, Gaussian, exponential, ARGUS, kernel estimates), treatment of nuisance parameters, and the estimator used for branching-ratio confidence intervals or limits (profile likelihood, CLs, Feldman–Cousins)?

How are detector acceptance, reconstruction/selection efficiencies and trigger inefficiencies determined and corrected in ATLAS B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− measurements — including the use of MC-derived acceptances, data-driven scale factors from control channels (J/ψ→μ+μ−, Υ→μ+μ−, B→J/ψK), tag-and-probe methods, trigger efficiency maps, reweighting procedures, and the validation/closure tests and systematic uncertainties assigned?

Which detector-related systematics (muon identification, trigger efficiencies, mass resolution, background modeling, luminosity) dominate the ATLAS experimental error budget for the measured B_s0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fractions, and what are their reported magnitudes?
sub_answers.text:
The ATLAS muon spectrometer is designed to measure muon momenta with a resolution of 4% at 100 GeV/c and about 10% at 1 TeV/c track momentum [d12480s0p0].
The muon precision detectors provide approximately 50 micron tracking resolution to a pseudo-rapidity of 2.7 [d12480s0p0].
ATLAS has deployed small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers to increase rate capability by about an order of magnitude compared to the previous MDT chambers [d36328s0p0].
Upgrades and new precision drift-tube chambers achieved sense wire positioning accuracies of about 5 microns in serial production [d31798s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Quantify how uncertainties in the b-hadron production fractions (f_s, f_d), b-quark fragmentation functions, and related acceptance corrections propagate into ATLAS’s extracted B_s0 and B0 branching ratios; which of these inputs contributes the largest fractional uncertainty?
sub_answers.text:
The ATLAS and LHC detector programs have pursued upgrades and calibrations to preserve muon reconstruction performance in higher-rate environments relevant for b-hadron measurements [d36328s0p0].
Muon reconstruction and trigger software performance in CMS was validated to meet design specifications and be well reproduced by simulation, illustrating the importance of simulation benchmarking for acceptance and efficiency corrections [d43425s0p0].
Measured and simulated muon rates at nearby experiments agree within about 10–15%, demonstrating the level of agreement achievable for flux and background simulations that inform acceptance corrections [d121223s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the numerical theoretical inputs used when converting signal yields into branching ratios (decay constants f_Bs, f_B, bag parameters, CKM elements, short-distance Wilson coefficients) and give the quoted uncertainties or error correlations ATLAS cites for each in their B→μ+μ− interpretation.
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS muon-system upgrades and construction efforts focused on improving spatial resolution, rate capability, and stability, which are prerequisites for precise acceptance and efficiency determination in rare dimuon searches [d36328s0p0].
High-precision detector calibration and optical monitoring systems provide position measurements with approximately 40 micron precision, supporting control of detector-alignment related systematic effects [d12480s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Compare ATLAS’s central values and uncertainties for B_s0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− with those from CMS and LHCb: where do their confidence intervals or likelihood contours disagree, and which analysis choices (normalization channel, fit model, event selection) drive those inter-experiment differences?
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS has conducted searches for narrow scalar resonances decaying to muon pairs using 36.1 fb^{-1} of 13 TeV data, setting cross-section times branching-ratio upper limits between roughly 1.6 and 44 fb depending on production mode and mass, which illustrates an example of an analysis chain from yield to physics limit in dimuon channels [d48617s0p0].
CMS muon detector performance studies report that their modified muon system met design specifications for spatial resolution, efficiency, and timing, which are the kinds of detector performance inputs compared across experiments when interpreting dimuon branching-fraction results [d43425s0p0].
The CMS RPC system provides redundancy to the muon trigger and contributes to both muon trigger and reconstruction, which affects inter-experiment differences in trigger and selection efficiency [d45889s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Detail which theory assumptions (choice of effective operator basis, inclusion/exclusion of scalar/pseudoscalar operators, assumptions of lepton-flavour universality, inputs from lattice QCD) are made in ATLAS interpretations of B→μ+μ− limits and explain how alternative assumptions would change the mapping from measured rates to constraints on new-physics couplings.
sub_answers.text:
ATLAS upgraded muon detectors and tracking precision to maintain performance under increased luminosity and background, enabling interpretations of rare dimuon rates that rely on calibrated detector response and lattice-QCD or theory inputs, though specific choices of effective operator basis or scalar/pseudoscalar operator inclusion are not detailed in the cited detector and performance documents [d36328s0p0].
Simulation frameworks validated against measured muon fluxes and detector performance benchmarks are used to design mitigation and to project performance into future high-luminosity running, which informs how theoretical constraints map from measured rates under different experimental assumptions [d121223s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which numerical bounds do ATLAS measurements of B_s0 → μ+μ− place on specific Wilson coefficients in the b→sℓℓ effective Hamiltonian (e.g., C9, C10, C9′, C10′, C_S, C_P and their complex phases), and how do those bounds compare to limits from LHCb and CMS?

In what way have ATLAS B_s0→μ+μ− results altered outcomes of global EFT fits performed with tools like Flavio, HEPfit or EOS that test lepton-flavor universality and scalar/pseudoscalar operators (for example shifts in best-fit values or changes in allowed regions for C9μ−C9e, C10, C_S, C_P)?
sub_answers.text: The combined CMS and LHCb analysis produced the first observation of the B0_s→μ+μ− decay with a significance exceeding six standard deviations [d25198s0p0]. The measured branching fractions are statistically compatible with Standard Model predictions [d25198s0p0]. The measurements impose stringent constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model, affecting global EFT fits that test lepton-flavor universality and scalar/pseudoscalar operators [d25198s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which specific classes and benchmark realizations of beyond-Standard-Model scenarios (for example MSSM/CMSSM regions with large tanβ, Type-II 2HDM, Z′ models with flavor-changing bs couplings, and leptoquark representations such as S1 or U1) are directly excluded or strongly constrained by the ATLAS measurements of B_s→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fractions?
sub_answers.text: The measured B0_s→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fractions are statistically compatible with Standard Model predictions and therefore impose stringent constraints on several theories beyond the Standard Model [d25198s0p0]. The combined analysis produced the best measurement of the B0_s→μ+μ− branching fraction to date [d25198s0p0]. The analysis also provided evidence for the B0→μ+μ− decay with a statistical significance of three standard deviations [d25198s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do the ATLAS B_s→μ+μ− upper limits get propagated into world averages and combined constraints by groups such as HFLAV (formerly HFAG), PDG, or combined LHC combinations, and what methodology (treatment of correlations, likelihood combinations, use of nuisance parameters) is used to incorporate ATLAS results into those experimental averages?
sub_answers.text: A joint measurement by CMS and LHCb produced the first observation of B0_s→μ+μ− and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far, and these results were obtained from combined proton-proton collision data collected in 2011 and 2012 [d25198s0p0]. The combined analysis technique produced evidence for B0→μ+μ− at the three standard deviation level [d25198s0p0].

Which ATLAS algorithms and track- or muon-system-based selections are used to identify muons and reconstruct low-momentum muon pairs in rare B→μ+μ− decay studies, and what versions/configurations of the muon spectrometer reconstruction (e.g., combined, standalone, segment-tagged) are cited in relevant ATLAS papers or performance notes?
sub_answers.text:
The ATLAS muon spectrometer measures muon momenta with about 4% resolution at 100 GeV/c rising to about 10% at 1 TeV/c track momentum [d12480s0p0].
The spectrometer uses precision tracking chambers providing roughly 50 μm tracking resolution up to pseudo-rapidity 2.7 and an optical monitoring system that measures detector positions with about 40 μm precision [d12480s0p0].
ATLAS combines precision Muon Drift Tube (MDT) chambers and upgraded small-diameter MDT (sMDT) chambers together with trigger chambers to improve acceptance for precision muon momentum measurement and triggering, and fast MDT read-out and a fast MDT track reconstruction algorithm have been developed for low-latency trigger decisions [d31941s0p0][d31798s0p0][d36328s0p0][d32191s0p0].
